The Client 

Blaze Engineering and Sheetmetal Fabrication Pty Ltd is a metal fabrication and engineering business based in Tullamarine, VIC, specialising in sheet metal fabrication, welding, metal assembly, and engineered manufacturing solutions.  

They are seeking an experienced Welder (First Class) to join their team in Tullamarine, VIC. 

 

The Role 

The Welder (First Class) is responsible for fabricating, assembling, and repairing metal components and structures using a range of welding and fabrication techniques. 

This is a full-time position with an annual salary of $78,000 to $82,000 plus superannuation. 

 

The Responsibilities 

Select and prepare appropriate welding equipment, consumables, and materials for welding operations. 

Read and interpret technical drawings, blueprints, welding procedures, and specifications to determine welding requirements. 

Mark out and cut metal sections and components using metal-cutting machinery. 

Shape and bend metal sections and plates using machine tools. 

Set up and operate MIG welding equipment to weld, join, and repair metal components and structures. 

Position and secure workpieces to ensure accurate alignment and welding in accordance with specifications. 

Perform welding operations on various metal components while maintaining required quality and safety standards. 

Inspect completed welds to ensure compliance with specified dimensions, quality requirements, and welding standards. 

Repair defective welds and damaged metal components through grinding, gouging, and rewelding processes. 

Perform weld finishing activities, including grinding and dressing welds to achieve the required finish and appearance. 

Use measuring and testing instruments to verify weld quality, accuracy, and compliance with specifications. 

Carry out welding repairs and maintenance on metal structures, machinery, equipment, and related components. 

Clean and prepare metal surfaces before and after welding to ensure quality. 

Conduct routine maintenance and basic troubleshooting of welding equipment to ensure safe and efficient operation. 

Follow workplace health and safety procedures, welding safety requirements, and relevant industry regulations at all times. 

Work collaboratively with supervisors, engineers, inspectors, and other trades personnel to complete welding tasks efficiently. 

Maintain accurate records of welding activities, inspections, repairs, materials used, and work completed. 

 

The Requirements 

Certificate IV in Engineering or equivalent qualification 

Minimum 1.5 years’ experience as a Welder (First Class) or within metal fabrication environments 

Minimum 1.5 years’ experience performing MIG welding across structural steel and fabricated metal components 

Minimum 1.5 years’ experience interpreting engineering drawings, fabrication plans, and technical specifications 

At least 1.5 years’ experience operating fabrication machinery, welding equipment, and metalworking tools 

At least 1.5 years’ experience assembling, repairing, and finishing fabricated metal products to engineering standards 

Sound knowledge of a range of welding techniques, including TIG, flux-cored and manual metal arc welding, and their application in metal fabrication. 

Strong knowledge of welding procedures, fabrication methods, and metal finishing techniques 

Ability to identify welding defects, dimensional inconsistencies, and fabrication issues accurately 

Strong understanding of workplace safety procedures, fabrication compliance standards, and workshop operations 

Good communication skills and ability to work effectively within fabrication and engineering teams 

High attention to detail and commitment to precision workmanship

Job Title: Control Room Operator (Engineering Technologist ANZSCO 233914)
Company: Scidell Pty Ltd, an associated entity of Multicom Resources Pty Ltd
Location: St Elmo Site, Julia Creek QLD 4823, Australia
Employment Type: Permanent, Full-time

About the company:
Our client Scidell Pty Ltd is a newly formed scientific delivery alliancing company of Multicom Resources Pty Ltd. Scidell is dedicated to providing cost-effective solutions to Multicom Resources, its foundation alliance client, while also seeking opportunities to expand its services.

Multicom Resources is a Queensland-based exploration and minerals refining company focused on discovering and developing world-class mineral deposits. Among its key projects is the Saint Elmo Project, located in the Northwest Minerals Province of Queensland. This project is advancing the production of vanadium and high-purity alumina, essential resources for global technology manufacturers.

About the role:
As a Control Room Operator at Scidell, you will play a vital role in the operations of the Saint Elmo Mine's mineral processing plant. Reporting to the Plant Manager, this position involves monitoring and optimizing plant equipment using advanced HMI systems and automated controls. You’ll be instrumental in ensuring plant safety, efficiency, and compliance with production goals and regulatory standards.
This is a full-time role operating on a rotating roster.

Key Requirements:
-A minimum of 1 year of experience in a similar role, such as a Control Room Operator, or within a related field, such as mining or mineral processing.
-A demonstrated ability to quickly learn and apply knowledge about process plant operations.
-Proficiency in operating and troubleshooting HMI and automated control systems (e.g., DCS, SCADA).
-Strong problem-solving skills to assess process disturbances and implement corrective actions effectively.
-Attention to detail to monitor plant conditions and identify operational changes.
-A commitment to maintaining safety and compliance with health, safety, and environmental standards.

Key Responsibilities:
-Monitor and control plant equipment using modern HMI and automated systems to ensure efficient and safe operations.
-Detect and respond to changes in process conditions and troubleshoot equipment issues.
-Collaborate with field operators and maintenance personnel to resolve process disruptions.
-Coordinate plant start-ups, shutdowns, and emergency operations to minimize downtime.
-Review plant performance data to identify trends and implement process optimizations.
-Support continuous improvement initiatives and contribute to enhancing plant efficiency.
-Maintain compliance with safety protocols and assist in training new operators.

Why Join Us?
Scidell offers a unique opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge mineral processing projects while working in a supportive and collaborative environment. Be part of a team that values innovation, safety, and excellence in delivering critical minerals to global markets.

How to Apply:
If you're ready to be part of a dynamic team at Scidell Pty Ltd, dedicated to innovation and excellence, we’d love to hear from you! Please submit your application, ensuring you highlight your relevant experience and qualifications.

Scidell Pty Ltd is an equal-opportunity employer, committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds. While we appreciate every application, please note that only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

result.description: square steel pty ltd  About the Role  Square Steel Pty Ltd is seeking a motivated and experienced  Production Engineer  to join our growing team. The successful applicant will play a key role in planning, coordinating, and improving manufacturing operations to ensure products are delivered efficiently, safely, and to the highest quality standards. The position requires close collaboration with engineering, production, procurement, and quality teams to optimise production processes and support continuous improvement initiatives.  Key Responsibilities   Plan, organise and coordinate manufacturing and production activities to achieve project deadlines and operational targets.  Develop, review and implement efficient production methods, workflows and manufacturing processes.  Analyse production performance and identify opportunities to improve productivity, quality and resource utilisation.  Interpret engineering drawings, specifications and technical documentation to support manufacturing operations.  Determine material requirements and coordinate with procurement to ensure timely availability of production resources.  Investigate production issues, identify root causes and implement practical engineering solutions to minimise downtime.  Monitor manufacturing activities to ensure compliance with engineering specifications, Australian Standards and company quality requirements.  Work closely with drafting, fabrication, installation and quality assurance teams to ensure efficient project delivery.  Prepare production schedules and allocate resources to maximise operational efficiency.  Evaluate manufacturing equipment, production systems and work methods, recommending improvements where appropriate.  Support the implementation of quality assurance procedures and continuous improvement initiatives.  Ensure manufacturing operations comply with workplace health and safety policies and relevant legislative requirements.  Maintain accurate engineering and production records and prepare technical reports as required.   Essential Requirements   Bachelor's degree or higher qualification in  Mechanical Engineering, Production Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering , or a closely related discipline.  Minimum  3-4 years of relevant post-qualification experience  as a Production Engineer or in a similar engineering role.  Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, production planning and continuous improvement principles.  Ability to interpret engineering drawings and technical specifications.  Knowledge of quality management systems and Australian Standards.  Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.  Strong organisational, communication and teamwork abilities.  Proficiency in Microsoft Office and engineering/manufacturing software.   Desirable Skills   Experience within the steel fabrication, structural steel, light gauge steel (LGS), or manufacturing industry.  Experience with ERP/MRP production planning systems.  Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma or other process improvement methodologies.  Experience in production scheduling, material planning and quality assurance.   What We Offer   Full-time permanent employment.  Competitive remuneration package.  Supportive and collaborative work environment.  Opportunity to work on diverse manufacturing projects.  Career development and professional growth opportunities.   If you have the required qualifications, technical expertise and a passion for manufacturing excellence, we encourage you to apply.  About Company     Square Steel Pty Ltd  is a South Australian company that designs, manufactures, and supplies lightgauge steel framing systems for residential and commercial construction. The company provides inhouse CAD design, manufacturing, and delivery, delivering durable, code-compliant steel framing solutions.
